thread:
leo: Follow-up to the service-lattice RFC. We need a pragmatic plan to collapse ~8 low-traffic endpoints that live across 4 services into a single lightweight facade (lattice-facade) to reduce operational churn. Main risks: owner churn, latent compatibility, and hidden cache dependencies. cc @anika @taylor

anika: Agree this is overdue. Two important constraints: keep per-tenant isolation, and don't increase tail latencies for hot paths. Suggest start with a read-only consolidation first, then tackle write-side.

taylor: For compatibility we should expose the same APIs but implement an adapter layer that delegates to the original service until cutover. Adapter responsibilities: header normalization, legacy param mapping, and per-tenant routing. Keep adapters as thin as possible.

may: Cache dependencies note: some callers rely on warming behavior from service A. We must detect call-sites that expect warm caches. Proposal: instrument a cache-warm metric and flag callers returning >20% cache-miss for 7d window. Those callers require special handling (sticky routing or prewarm).

leo: Proposed phases:
- Phase 0: discovery sprint — enumerate endpoints, owners, traffic profiles, cache characteristics, and SLAs (1 week)
- Phase 1: facade + adapter prototype in staging, proxy old calls, no cutover (2 weeks)
- Phase 2: read-path consolidation (shadowing) for 72h, collect metrics and semantic checks
- Phase 3: write-path dual-write for owners who require strong consistency (configurable), plus background reconciliation for eventual writers
- Phase 4: deprecate legacy endpoints with 8-week compatibility window

infra-bot: Prototype deployment created -> env=staging cohort=proxy-1% id=canary-1797654321-1 :satellite:

taylor: Automation: add a feature-flag per-endpoint and a rollout orchestrator that evaluates gates. Example gates: error_rate < 0.5% AND p95_latency <= baseline*1.25 AND cache_miss_rate_delta <= 5% AND semantic_regression <= 1.5%.

anika: Ownership + action items: leo (architect) to own discovery sprint doc; taylor (platform) to build adapter template and rollout automations; may (data) to run cache-warm analysis and list callers that need special handling; infra to provision facade infra and cost estimate. Timeline: discovery this week, prototype next week.

may: Cost note: consolidating reduces cross-service idle CPU but adds one more hot path on the facade. Expect net -6% infra cost for the set, but facade should be horizontally autoscaled with tight CPU limits. I'll send an estimate.

leo: Runbook snippet:
```nIf facade.p95 > baseline*1.5 OR error_rate > 1% for 15min -> toggle feature_flag for affected endpoint to 0 and notify #oncall
Rollback: curl -X POST $FF/toggle?env=prod&flag=lattice_facade_endpoint_<id>&value=0
```n
anika: Also add a lightweight consumer contract test that runs in CI for each endpoint mapping to catch subtle param/enum changes. Will help prevent semantic regressions.

leo: OK I'll open the discovery doc and share a checklist. If no objections by EOD Fri we start the sprint Mon. Thanks all :facepunch:
